rationale: A wins because it knows where the story stops and where the proof begins. Its strongest line, "whether the 10% sits on top of, or absorbs, the Apple/Google in-app-purchase cut," is exactly the reporter-killer question; B's "Millions of Unpaid Gaming Community Managers Just Got a Business Model" walks straight into unsupported scale and labor claims. B has usable shapes, but it decorates too much. A does the adult PR work: sharp angles, named proof gaps, fewer fairy lights.
gaps_in_A: "Discord servers have historically been free communities" is plausible background, but it is not in the supplied update. Keep it as a hypothesis unless Discord can substantiate it.

"Patreon, Twitch, Geneva" and "Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" add outside comparison points not supplied in the update. Useful context, but the set should mark them as proof to verify, not quiet facts.
The third angle needs a harder human proof floor. "A named server owner" is right, but without one the angle is still more analysis than story.
gaps_in_B: "Millions of Unpaid Gaming Community Managers Just Got a Business Model" invents both scale and unpaid status. That headline needs evidence or a bin.
"first real monetization product" is not in the update and is likely wrong given Discord's existing revenue products. That is the kind of overclaim that gets a pitch deleted.
"in range with Patreon and Twitch" adds unsupplied competitor-rate claims. If you want that comparison, prove it before it touches a journalist.

The fourth angle, "Discord Was Built for Gamers. Its Creator Subscription Launch Is a Bet It Can Be Patreon," overlaps the creator/community monetization angle and relies on broad platform-identity theater instead of a new fact.
